brief.headline: The blocking workload (adhoc_reporting) is not in the workload registry (BIZ-2). Per invariant I4, nobody can price the interruption of an unknown workload. The trade-off evidence (BIZ-5) confirms the cost of interrupting is unknown. A human owner must decide whether to terminate an unregistered workload.
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 105526 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 27% over 30s (88/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,493/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 105526) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,493/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Checkout success collapsed to 27% over 30s (BIZ-4) with $13,493/min at risk, exceeding the 60s tolerance (BIZ-1). The blocker (pid 105526) is idle in transaction for 4s (DB-1), has no registry entry (BIZ-2), no change-calendar protection (BIZ-3), and no protected settlements (DB-2). However, I4 forbids accepting termination of an unknown workload because its interrupt cost cannot be priced. The trade-off analysis (BIZ-5) explicitly states interrupt cost is unknown. Escalation to a human owner is required.

audit.report: An unknown adhoc_reporting session (pid 105526) held a lock idle-in-transaction for 4 seconds, blocking checkout and degrading success to 27% over 30 seconds with $13,493/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting due to unknown interrupt cost, but switched to terminate after checkout collapsed past the 60-second tolerance window. The Continuity Guardian escalated per invariant I4 because the workload was not in the registry, making its interruption cost unpriceable. No automated action executed; the incident was escalated to on-call after 50.4 seconds.
audit.root_cause: An unregistered adhoc_reporting workload held a lock idle-in-transaction, blocking checkout and triggering an escalation because its interruption cost could not be priced per invariant I4.
lessons: Register all adhoc_reporting workloads with owner, replayability, and interrupt-cost metadata so the guardians can price termination without human escalation.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian correctly gathered evidence and reversed its proposal when business impact escalated, but the Continuity Guardian was forced to escalate by invariant I4 rather than negotiate a trade-off, wasting the single round on a policy block instead of a risk decision.
follow_ups: On-call to confirm whether pid 105526 was terminated manually and document the actual interrupt cost for adhoc_reporting.
Engineering to add adhoc_reporting to the workload registry with owner, SLA, and replayability tags within 48 hours.
Platform to implement idle-in-transaction timeout enforcement on the checkout database role.

events.title: 3 candidate actions enumerated from observed evidence

candidates.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting, pid 105526) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
Hand the decision to the owning team with a decision brief.

proposal.rationale: The blocker (pid 105526) has been idle in transaction for only 4.0s (DB-1). Checkout is degraded at 53% success (TEL-1) and 74% over 10s (BIZ-1), with $4,748/min at risk, but the business tolerates up to 60s of degradation (BIZ-1). Without knowing the workload's owner, replayability, interrupt policy, or whether it's in a protected change window, terminating risks data corruption or replay cost. The lock graph shows only 1 session directly blocked by this PID, suggesting limited blast radius. Waiting for the transaction to complete naturally is lower risk than blind termination.
proposal.expected_effect: If the blocker commits/rolls back within the next ~56s (within the 60s tolerance), locks release and checkout recovers automatically. If it persists beyond 60s, we'll need to escalate or terminate with better context.
proposal.risk_assessment: Checkout remains degraded during wait. If blocker holds locks beyond 60s tolerance, revenue impact increases. However, terminating an unknown batch_worker/adhoc_reporting workload could cause data inconsistency, require expensive replay, or violate change management policies.
